text: No road reaches High Bridge from outside the valley. Take the passenger ferry or a floatplane up Lake Chelan to Stehekin, then the seasonal shuttle bus about 11 miles up the Stehekin Valley Road to High Bridge at about 1,600 ft, where the Agnes Creek Trail (PCT) starts.

There is no road to this trailhead from outside: reach Stehekin at the head of Lake Chelan by the Lady of the Lake ferry, floatplane or trail, then ride the valley shuttle, bike or walk 11 miles up the Stehekin Valley Road from Stehekin Landing to High Bridge, around 1,600 ft. Arrange any overnight backcountry permit before you travel, since there is no permit office in Stehekin.

pins.name: High Bridge / Agnes Creek Trailhead (Stehekin Valley Road)

text: No road reaches this trailhead. Get to Stehekin from Chelan on the Lake Chelan passenger ferry (Lady Express about 2.5 hours, Lady II about 4 hours) or by floatplane, then ride the scheduled Stehekin Valley shuttle bus up-valley to High Bridge at 1,700 ft, which is the end of the road and the start of the Agnes Creek Trail. Both the ferry and the shuttle run fixed, limited daily schedules and the

There is no road connection to this trailhead from outside the valley: reach Stehekin by the Lake Chelan ferry or floatplane, then take the Stehekin Valley Road or the NPS shuttle about eleven miles up-valley to the bridge. Plan the whole trip around the boat and shuttle timetable, because missing the last run means an extra night.

There is no road in. Take the passenger ferry or a floatplane up Lake Chelan to Stehekin, then ride the valley shuttle up the Stehekin Valley Road to High Bridge, and plan around both timetables. You need a free self-issue wilderness permit but no parking pass.

From Twisp, drive west up the Twisp River Road (FR 44) for 18.3 miles and bear left onto FR 4435. Cross the Twisp River in 0.3 mile, turn right after the bridge to stay on FR 4435, drive 1.1 miles upriver and turn left onto Spur 4435-015, reaching the trailhead in another 0.3 mile at about 3,100 ft. A free self-issued Lake Chelan-Sawtooth Wilderness permit is filled out at the kiosk.

pins.name: Arrow Creek switchback (Illabot Creek Road / FR-16)

text: Drive Highway 530 to Illabot Creek Road (FR-16) and follow it to the Arrow Creek switchback at about 2,220 ft. This is the trailhead, but not a formal one, so park on the road at the switchback and expect no lot and nothing signed. The boot path leaves the road roughly 20 yards west of the Arrow Creek crossing and follows the south bank of Illabot Creek upstream.

From Twisp, follow the Twisp River Road west about 22 miles; it becomes FR 44 and then gravel FR 4440. The Scatter Creek trailhead, at about 3,100 ft, is about 50 yards past the Slate Creek Trail sign. A Northwest Forest Pass or day pass is required to park; no wilderness permit is needed.

From Marblemount, drive 14.2 miles up Cascade River Road, then turn right onto FR-1570 (Kindy Creek Road) cross the wooden bridge over Kindy Creek, and continue about 2 miles up the rough spur to a small pullout near Vee Creek, at about 1,850 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is needed to park here. FR-1570 is washed out, so this is as far as you drive and the trip begins on foot up the blocked, brushy

From Marblemount, drive the Cascade River Road about 14.2 miles to the signed FR-1570 (Kindy Creek Road) junction and turn right. Cross the Cascade River on a concrete bridge and continue about 0.4 mile to a Y junction where the right fork is blocked by boulders. Park there, at roughly 1,150 to 1,300 feet - a long-standing washout on FR-1570 keeps most parties from driving any higher, so the route

Drive Cascade River Road roughly 14.2 miles from Marblemount and turn onto FR-1570, signed for Kindy Ridge and Found Lake, crossing the Cascade River. Park at the washout just past the washed-out culvert — a small pullout with room for four or five cars at about 1,250 ft. FR-1570 is impassable to vehicles beyond this point and the old spur is permanently closed, so the hike starts on the abandoned

Drive Cascade River Road to its end, about 22 to 23 miles from Marblemount, to the large parking lot at the Cascade Pass Trailhead at 3,600 feet. If you plan to stay overnight at Sahale Glacier Camp, note that the permit is quota-limited — get an early-access wilderness permit or a walk-up the day before at the Marblemount ranger station.

text: The trailhead is at the very end of Cascade River Road (FR-15), roughly 23 miles from Marblemount and about 3,600 feet in elevation. Any overnight camping beyond the trailhead requires a self-issue wilderness permit.

Follow Cascade River Road (Forest Road 15, paved then gravel) about 23 miles from Marblemount to its end at the Cascade Pass Trailhead, at roughly 3,600 feet inside North Cascades National Park. The road has washed out in several recent seasons below the trailhead, adding 2 to 6 miles of road walking each way when unrepaired, so check current conditions before you go. No parking pass is required h

Drive Cascade River Road 23.1 miles from Marblemount to the Cascade Pass Trailhead at about 3,600 ft; it is paved to start and gravel the rest of the way. The season here runs July through September and depends on Cascade River Road being open, so check that before you make the drive. Most parties climb this as one very long day from the lot, leaving the car around 2-3 am; if you would rather spli
From SR 20 at Marblemount, cross the Skagit River bridge onto Cascade River Road and follow it about 23 miles to its end at the Cascade Pass Trailhead lot, about 3,660 ft. The upper miles are gravel.

pins.name: Cascade Pass Trailhead (end of Cascade River Road)

text: The final miles of Cascade River Road out of Marblemount are unpaved and washboarded, and high clearance or AWD makes the drive to the road end considerably easier.

From SR-20 at Marblemount, cross the Skagit River and drive the Cascade River Road about 23 miles to its end at the Cascade Pass Trailhead, around 3,650 ft. The first 10 miles are paved and the rest is narrow gravel with potholes, steep near the top. Overnight stays in the park need a backcountry permit from the Marblemount Wilderness Information Center.

Drive Cascade River Road to its end at the Cascade Pass Trailhead, about 3,600 feet. The road washes out periodically, so confirm it is open all the way to the trailhead before you go. A North Cascades National Park wilderness permit is required for the overnight bivy this route involves.

pins.name: Boston Basin / Cascade River Road trailhead
Boston Basin Trailhead (Cascade River Road pullout)

text: The start is a small pullout on Cascade River Road at about mile 21.7, roughly 3,200 ft, opposite Johannesburg Mountain. There is no separate road trailhead for the Southeast Face — the face is reached from Boston Basin high camp, so this pullout is where you park. Camping in the basin needs an NPS wilderness permit registered through Marblemount, and the sites are popular enough to be worth arran

From SR 20 in Winthrop, turn onto White Avenue just after the bridge over the Methow River; it becomes Twin Lakes Road. At 1.3 miles turn right onto Wolf Creek Road, follow it 2.9 miles, then turn left onto Wildflower Road, which becomes FS Road 5005 in about half a mile. Follow the signs to the Wolf Creek Trail at the road end, about 4 miles on.

The Wolf Creek Trailhead is a large parking area at the end of FS Road 5505 (Left Fork Wolf Creek Road) above Winthrop, at about 2,900 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required; no wilderness permit is needed. Check current Wolf Creek Road conditions before you drive in. Most parties come mid-July through September, once the trail and the upper basins are snow-free.

From Winthrop, take SR 20 across the Methow River bridge at the south end of town and turn right onto Twin Lakes Road. In about 1.5 miles turn right onto Wolf Creek Road, then follow the signs onto gravel Forest Service road to the Wolf Creek Trailhead at about 2,900 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park.

text: From Marblemount, follow Cascade River Road south about 20 miles to the parking area near mile 20 — paved for the first 10 miles, gravel and washboard after that. Any overnight needs a free North Cascades backcountry permit, reserved in advance on Recreation.gov or drawn from the walk-up allocation in person at the Marblemount Wilderness Information Center.

From SR-20 in Marblemount, cross the Skagit River onto the Cascade River Road and drive about 20 miles, gravel after about mile 10, to the Eldorado climbers' parking near milepost 20 at about 2,100 ft. Overnight camps need a backcountry permit from the Marblemount Wilderness Information Center.

From SR 20 at Marblemount, cross the Skagit River bridge onto the Cascade River Road and drive about 20 miles east, paved for the first 10 then rough gravel, to the Eldorado parking area on the right near milepost 20. The climbers' trail leaves the road a short walk west of the lot. A park wilderness permit, picked up in person at the Wilderness Information Center in Marblemount, is required for a

Drive SR-20 (North Cascades Highway) to the Bridge Creek Trailhead near milepost 159, just over a mile east of Rainy Pass, and park in the paved lot on the north side of the highway at about 4,400 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, and an NPS backcountry permit is needed for overnight camping.

pins.name: Hidden Lake Trailhead (FR-1540 / Sibley Creek Road)

text: From Marblemount, follow Cascade River Road (FR-15) for about 10.2 paved miles, then turn onto FR-1540, Sibley Creek Road, and grind out 4.5 miles of rough gravel to the small Hidden Lake Trailhead at about 3,600 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park. Many parties sleep at the trailhead the night before rather than driving in before dawn. No permit is needed for a day climb; only overnig

Drive SR-20 over Washington Pass and continue east a short way down to the big hairpin turn below the pass, and park off the road at the curve at about 5,100 ft. The highway over the pass is closed in winter.

text: Park in the pullout at the hairpin turn on SR-20, a short distance east of Washington Pass at around 5,100 feet — the same roadside pullout used for the nearby West Route approach on Kangaroo Temple. No permit is required to park or climb from here.

text: Drive the North Cascades Highway (SR-20) to the long pullout on the north side of the road about 1.5 miles west of Washington Pass, roughly half a mile west of the Blue Lake Trailhead. The climbers' track leaves the east end of the pullout. SR-20 over Washington Pass is gated in winter, so this route's season begins when the highway reopens in spring.

pins.name: Rainy Pass / Lake Ann–Maple Pass Trailhead (Trail #740)

text: Drive SR-20 to Rainy Pass, about 52 miles east of Marblemount, and turn into the paved lot on the south side of the highway where the PCT crosses. Start on the Lake Ann/Maple Pass trail, which is well graded and heavily used the whole way to the pass.

pins.name: Rainy Pass / Lake Ann-Maple Pass Trailhead
Rainy Pass / Lake Ann-Maple Pass Trailhead

text: Drive SR-20 to Rainy Pass at about milepost 157.5 and turn into the Rainy Pass Picnic Site on the south side of the highway. The Lake Ann-Maple Pass trailhead (Trail 740) leaves from the paved lot at about 4,855 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park; day passes are sold at the trailhead.

Drive SR-20 (the North Cascades Highway) to the Blue Lake Trailhead on the south side of the highway just west of Washington Pass. The highway over the pass closes in winter. A Northwest Forest Pass or day fee is required to park.

Drive SR-20, the North Cascades Highway (closed over Washington Pass in winter), to the signed Blue Lake Trailhead near milepost 161, just west of Washington Pass: about 42 miles east of Newhalem, or about 30 miles west of Winthrop. Early in the season the lot may still hold snow. A Northwest Forest Pass or day pass is required.

Drive SR-20 (North Cascades Highway) to the Blue Lake Trailhead on the south side of the highway near milepost 161, just west of Washington Pass, at about 5,200 ft. Parking requires a Northwest Forest Pass.

From Winthrop, drive SR-20 west about 30 miles, over Washington Pass, to the signed Blue Lake Trailhead on the south side of the highway about a mile west of the pass, at roughly 5,400 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass, Interagency pass or day-use fee is required to park. SR-20 is gated over Washington Pass through the winter, so there is no drive-up access until it reopens in spring.

pins.name: SR-20 turnout below Le Petit Cheval (east of Washington Pass)
SR-20 turnout below Le Petit Cheval (east of Washington Pass)
SR-20 turnout below Le Petit Cheval (east of Washington Pass)

text: Drive SR-20 to the turnout below Le Petit Cheval, roughly 2 miles east of Washington Pass. Park in the turnout itself; the climbers' trail drops from its west or southwest end, so leave the car toward that end. The turnout is the trailhead — there is no side road, and the path down toward Early Winters Creek is unmarked apart from occasional cairns.

pins.name: SR-20 Pullout / Willow Creek approach start

text: From the summit of Washington Pass, drive SR-20 east about 3.5 miles and park in the long pullout at about 4,320 ft, on the road's right-hand side, where the Willow Creek valley opens up toward Big Snagtooth.

pins.name: Wine Spires / Burgundy Col pullout, SR-20

text: Drive SR-20 to the unsigned pullout near milepost 166, roughly four miles east of Washington Pass, at about 4,300 ft. There is no sign and no developed trailhead here, only a broad shoulder pullout, so watch your odometer. Check WSDOT before travelling: the highway is gated shut through the winter and reopens somewhere between mid-April and late June depending on snowpack and slide repair.
